requirements.statement: Each element with a script-controlled event handler, or another element in the page that performs the same action, can be reached and operated with the keyboard.

citations.quote: Chaque élément possédant un gestionnaire d’événement contrôlé par un script vérifie-t-il une de ces conditions (hors cas particuliers)
Vérifier que l’élément est accessible au moyen du clavier :
Sinon, vérifier qu’un élément accessible par le clavier permettant de réaliser la même action est présent dans la page.

routes.statement: The element itself is reachable with Tab and activated with Enter, or, for a complex action, usable with other keys such as the arrow keys.

citations.quote: L’élément est accessible par le clavier et tout dispositif de pointage
Il est atteignable avec la touche de tabulation (tab) ;
Si l’élément gère une action complexe, il est utilisable avec le clavier (généralement avec les touches de direction).

routes.statement: Another element in the page, reachable and operable with the keyboard, performs the same action.

citations.quote: Un élément accessible par le clavier et tout dispositif de pointage permettant de réaliser la même action est présent dans la page.
Sinon, vérifier qu’un élément accessible par le clavier permettant de réaliser la même action est présent dans la page.

routes.statement: On the keyboard side only: where focus handling is too complex or unstable for Tab, arrow keys and Enter, keyboard shortcuts that are documented, work and respect criterion 12.10 make the element usable from the keyboard; pointer use is not covered by this route and stays with the pointer requirement.

citations.entry: Accessible et activable par le clavier et tout dispositif de pointage
citations.quote: Dans ce cas, la mise à disposition de raccourcis clavier peut être la seule solution pour rendre le composant utilisable.

citations.entry: Accessible et activable par le clavier et tout dispositif de pointage
citations.quote: Le critère ne peut être considéré comme conforme qu’à la condition que les raccourcis clavier utilisés soient correctement documentés, qu’ils soient fonctionnels et qu’ils respectent le critère 12.10.

exceptions.statement: The functionality depends on an event handler with no universal equivalent, such as free-hand drawing; the criterion is then not applicable.

citations.quote: la fonctionnalité dépend de l’utilisation d’un gestionnaire d’événement sans équivalent universel ; par exemple, une application de dessin à main levée ne pourra pas être rendue contrôlable au clavier. Dans ces situations, le critère est non applicable.

requirements.statement: Each element with a script-controlled event handler, or another element in the page that performs the same action, can be reached and operated with any pointing device.

citations.quote: Vérifier que l’élément est accessible par tout dispositif de pointage (souris, toucher, stylet…).
Sinon, vérifier qu’un élément accessible au moyen d’un dispositif de pointage et permettant de réaliser la même action est présent dans la page.

routes.statement: The element itself can take focus and be activated with a pointer press.

citations.quote: L’élément est accessible par le clavier et tout dispositif de pointage

citations.entry: Accessible et activable par le clavier et tout dispositif de pointage
citations.quote: lorsque l’utilisateur peut enclencher, indifféremment, l’action prévue par le composant d’interface par une pression du pointeur ou la touche entrée du clavier

routes.statement: Another element in the page, usable with a pointing device, performs the same action.

citations.quote: permettant de réaliser la même action est présent dans la page.

rationale.text: The wording and the methodology disagree on how the two conditions combine. The wording lists two conditions, each about one element usable by keyboard and by pointer: the element itself, or one equivalent element that has both capabilities. Methodology steps 2 to 5 check the keyboard and the pointer separately, each with its own fallback to an equivalent element, so the keyboard equivalent and the pointer equivalent may be two different controls. A two-control case separates the readings: a div with a click handler that Tab cannot reach, and elsewhere a button performing the same action that is shown only while it has keyboard focus, so no pointer can reach it. The methodology validates it (pointer through the div, keyboard through the button); the wording fails it (neither element has both capabilities). The entry follows the methodology's split into a keyboard requirement and a pointer requirement, and the disagreement is recorded here unresolved. The split is the more permissive reading: a fault under it is a fault under the wording too, but its no_fault is not, so no pass may rest on it until the reading is ruled on. The glossary adds documented keyboard shortcuts as a way to make a component usable from the keyboard. That route is placed under the keyboard requirement only: the glossary's note concerns focus handling with Tab, the arrow keys and Enter, and says nothing of pointing devices, so pointer use still has to be met through the pointer requirement. Nothing here can be resolved by code. Whether another element performs the same action is judgment. Whether a complex widget is usable with the arrow keys, and whether shortcuts are documented and working, needs keyboard work and judgment. The particular case, a handler with no universal equivalent, is judgment too, and it has no mechanical precondition a check could rule out. No axe rule is tagged. I registered one evidence check: elements with a pointer or keyboard listener attached directly to them that Tab cannot reach. Its fault only shows the first keyboard route fails for that element; an equivalent element or shortcuts may exist, so it is evidence only and partial (listeners delegated to an ancestor cannot be attributed). The entry stays at none. Applicability is judgment: code sees directly attached listeners but not which elements a delegated listener serves, and the particular case needs judgment. Needs lists keyboard, since the methodology reaches and activates elements with Tab, Enter and the arrow keys. Pointer testing is also required but has no prerequisite of its own.
